title: Pascal Minus-One GCD
headline: Lean/Mathlib proofs of the restricted binomial-gcd valuation branches needed for complete prime-by-prime formulas at moduli 3, 4 and 6.
description: This project studies $G(N;m)=\gcd\{\binom Nk:0<k<N,\ m\mid k\}$. The repository now formally proves the $p\equiv-1\pmod m$ valuation theorem, the complementary $p\equiv1\pmod m$ branch used by the project, a common prime-power scaling theorem, and complete prime-by-prime valuation corollaries for $m=3,4,6$. The Lean source contains no theorem placeholders; finite Python checks remain regression evidence rather than substitutes for proof.
verification: Lean-verified theorem layer: minus-one valuation, plus-one valuation, scaling, and complete modulus 3, 4 and 6 valuation corollaries. Project Lean sources have zero explicit sorry, admit, or replacement axiom declarations; CI checks the build, regression tests, reference sweep, and zero-sorry gate.
attribution: John Fairfax-Ball maintains the repository and its Lean formalisation. Mathlib supplies Kummer's theorem and supporting digit machinery. The plus-one direction has known prior art and is not claimed as new here. The repository makes no publication-level novelty claim for the minus-one result without a separate source-level literature audit.
